findings.description: Direct inspection of all eleven current V151 images shows no legible pleat rhythm in the neutral/front/back/side/arm views after the declared hem fold relief increase from 30 mm to 40 mm. The skirt still reads as a broad, smooth/faceted A-line shell, with rigid apron-like side transitions and an uneven hard hem; the parameter-only change did not visibly resolve the garment-surface defect.

Crouch and sit still expose hard-edged shorts/thigh-cover shells across the upper legs while the skirt lifts away behind the thighs. Current pose-matched coverage is overskirt 0.267 per side in sit and 0.371 per side in crouch; shorts cover 0.638 in sit and 0.642 in crouch per side. These geometric diagnostics do not establish fit.
Angular triangular patches and abrupt surface transitions remain visible across the torso and waist/hip in the current V151 front, three-quarter, side, neutral and arm-cross views.

The current V151 prone image still shows garment and limbs intersecting/overlapping into a compact pile around pelvis and chest; silhouette and surface continuity are unacceptable in this required pose.

nextAction: Keep candidate REJECTED and prototype-only. The V151 30 mm to 40 mm authored hem-relief experiment did not make pleat structure visually legible, so do not repeat scalar amplitude tuning. Change the panel construction/topology or pleat profile so fold crests/valleys read as garment folds while preserving seams and armature deformation. Separately redesign shorts/thigh-cover panel cut and coverage for crouch/sit, correct torso/waist surface artifacts, and address prone intersections. Rebuild and directly inspect all eleven required views after each geometry change. Fit, UV, materials, Shape Keys, Unity, VRChat, package and release remain independent unverified gates.
